B13C029.summary: Matanga, born to a Chandala mother, spends a thousand years in penance trying to become a Brahmana. Sakra (Indra) tells him that someone of his birth can never reach that status, and Matanga, grieving, pushes his austerities until he collapses. Sakra then grants him other boons, and Matanga dies. The chapter is used to show that Brahmana status is very high and cannot be won by penance alone.

scenes.B13C029S01: Matanga's long penance, Sakra's refusal to grant Brahmana status, and Matanga's bitter reply.
scenes.B13C029S02: Matanga asks for other boons, Sakra grants him fame, Matanga dies, and Bhishma draws the moral.

shots.B13C029S01H01: Matanga refuses Indra's advice and spends a thousand years in penance, standing on one foot.
shots.B13C029S01H02: After another thousand years, Matanga asks Indra why he still has not won Brahmana status.
shots.B13C029S01H03: Indra says a Chandala can never become a Brahmana; Matanga goes to Prayaga and Gaya and penances until he collapses, and Indra catches him.
shots.B13C029S01H04: Indra explains that Brahmana status is out of Matanga's reach, describes its honour and dangers, and asks him to choose another boon.
shots.B13C029S01H05: Matanga protests that Indra is wounding a man already dead, blames his mother for his birth, and asks for some other boon.
shots.B13C029S02H01: Bhishma says Indra again urges Matanga to name a boon.
shots.B13C029S02H02: Matanga asks for the power to change shape, fly, enjoy pleasures, be honoured by Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, and win lasting fame.
shots.B13C029S02H03: Indra grants him fame as the deity of a verse measure and worship from women, then leaves; Matanga dies and goes to a high place, and Bhishma concludes that Brahmana status is high and comes only by birth.

B13C030.summary: Yudhishthira asks how the king Vitahavya became a Brahmana, since Viswamitra did as well. Bhishma tells how Vitahavya's hundred sons overran the kingdom of Kasi, and how Divodasa's son Pratarddana defeated them in battle. Vitahavya fled to the sage Bhrigu, who protected him and made him a Brahmana by his word alone. The chapter ends with the family line from Gritsamada down to Saunaka, which shows the Brahmana descent of this house.

scenes.B13C030S01: Yudhishthira's question, the wars between the Haihayas and the kings of Kasi, Pratarddana's victory, Vitahavya's elevation by Bhrigu, and the genealogy.

shots.B13C030S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how Vitahavya gained Brahmana status, since Viswamitra did too, and whether it came by a boon or by penance.
shots.B13C030S01H02: Bhishma begins the story: Haihaya's hundred sons take Kasi from Haryyaswa and later defeat Sudeva, and Divodasa rebuilds Benares and fights them for a thousand days.
shots.B13C030S01H03: Divodasa loses his army and treasury, flees his capital, and seeks refuge with the sage Bharadwaja.
shots.B13C030S01H04: Divodasa pleads for protection; Bharadwaja arranges a sacrifice that brings a son, Pratarddana, who quickly masters the Vedas and arms and defeats the Vitahavya sons; Vitahavya flees to Bhrigu, and Pratarddana follows him there.
shots.B13C030S01H05: Pratarddana asks for Vitahavya, but Bhrigu says no Kshatriya is in his hermitage; Pratarddana leaves, and Vitahavya becomes a Brahmana by Bhrigu's word. The text then gives the line from Gritsamada through Ruru and Pramadvara to Saunaka.

B13C031.summary: Yudhishthira asks which men in the three worlds deserve reverent worship. Bhishma tells an old story in which Narada worships a large group of Brahmanas, and Krishna asks him whom he honours. Narada names the Brahmanas he reveres by their virtues and says those who keep such virtues escape every calamity. Bhishma closes by urging Yudhishthira to honour the gods, the ancestors, the Brahmanas and guests.

scenes.B13C031S01: Yudhishthira's question, Krishna's question to Narada, Narada's list of revered Brahmanas, and Bhishma's advice to Yudhishthira.

shots.B13C031S01H01: Yudhishthira asks which men in the three worlds deserve reverence and says he never tires of hearing such talk.
shots.B13C031S01H02: Bhishma introduces an old dialogue in which Narada worships many Brahmanas, and Krishna asks whom he is honouring.
shots.B13C031S01H03: Narada names the Brahmanas he honours and lists their virtues, such as penance, Vedic study, self-restraint, charity and hospitality, and says those who keep them cross every calamity.
shots.B13C031S01H04: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira to honour the deities, the ancestors, the Brahmanas and guests, and says this brings a good end.

B13C032.summary: Yudhishthira asks what merit comes from protecting living beings who seek shelter. Bhishma answers with the story of a pigeon chased by a hawk, which takes refuge in the lap of king Vrishadarbha. The hawk demands the pigeon as its food, and the king ends up offering flesh cut from his own body, which the text presents as the highest act of protection. The story ends with the king's reward in heaven and the claim that hearing it cleanses sin.

scenes.B13C032S01: Yudhishthira's question, the pigeon's plea to King Vrishadarbha, the hawk's objection, and the king's first offer of other meat.
scenes.B13C032S02: The hawk's demand for the king's own flesh, the king's sacrifice, his reward in heaven, and the moral for Yudhishthira.

shots.B13C032S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what merit comes from protecting creatures that beg for shelter.
shots.B13C032S01H02: Bhishma tells of a pigeon chased by a hawk that takes shelter in King Vrishadarbha's lap, and the king comforts it.
shots.B13C032S01H03: The hawk argues that the pigeon is its rightful food and that the king's authority does not extend to birds of the sky.
shots.B13C032S01H04: The king is struck with wonder but does not dismiss the hawk's words, and he turns to answer.
shots.B13C032S01H05: The king offers the hawk other meats such as beef, boar, deer or buffalo, and says he will not abandon a creature that sought his protection.
shots.B13C032S02H01: The hawk refuses other meat, says hawks eat pigeons by natural law, and asks for the king's own flesh equal in weight to the pigeon.
shots.B13C032S02H02: The king cuts his own flesh to weigh against the pigeon; the palace grieves, the earth trembles, and the king finally climbs onto the scale. The gods arrive, showers of nectar and flowers fall, and the king rises to heaven. The text then draws its moral and says reciting the story cleanses sin.

B13C033.summary: Yudhishthira asks which act a king should put first to win happiness in this world and the next. Bhishma answers that honouring learned Brahmanas is the foremost duty of a king. He describes the many kinds of Brahmanas, their great power, and the ruin that comes to those who speak against them. He ends by saying that no one can truly defeat the Brahmanas.

scenes.B13C033S01: Yudhishthira's question and Bhishma's long answer on the king's duty to honour and protect the Brahmanas.

shots.B13C033S01H01: Yudhishthira asks which act a king should put first, and which one brings happiness in both worlds.
shots.B13C033S01H02: Bhishma says that worshipping Brahmanas is the king's foremost duty, describes the varied kinds of Brahmanas and their powers, notes that insulting them brings downfall, and ends by saying no one can overcome them.

B13C034.summary: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira that Brahmanas must be honoured because the kingdom's peace and the gods' favour depend on them. He lists the benefits of feeding and supporting them and the defeats of Kshatriyas who fought them. He then gives a dialogue in which the Earth tells Vasudeva (Krishna) that serving Brahmanas cleanses sin and that harming them leads to ruin. Bhishma closes by urging Yudhishthira to honour the superior Brahmanas.

scenes.B13C034S01: Bhishma's case for honouring Brahmanas, the Earth's teaching to Vasudeva on serving them, and Bhishma's closing advice to Yudhishthira.

shots.B13C034S01H01: Bhishma says Brahmanas must be revered and supported, that the kingdom's peace depends on it, and that the Kshatriyas who fought them were defeated; he then introduces a talk between Vasudeva and the Earth.
shots.B13C034S01H02: Vasudeva asks the Earth by what conduct a householder can cleanse all his sins.
shots.B13C034S01H03: The Earth replies that serving Brahmanas cleanses and brings prosperity, fame and self-knowledge, and that speaking against them brings ruin.
shots.B13C034S01H04: Bhishma says Krishna praised the Earth's words and urges Yudhishthira to always worship the superior Brahmanas.

B13C035.summary: Bhishma says Brahmanas are worthy of worship by birth, because they are the mouths of the gods and guides of all creatures. He quotes verses attributed to Brahma that set out the Brahmanas' duties and the rewards of study, sacrifice and self-restraint. He ends by describing their great power and urging the king to honour them with gifts and service. The section closes with a note that the parva continues in another volume.

scenes.B13C035S01: Bhishma's praise of the Brahmanas, Brahma's verses on their duties, and the closing notes of the section.

shots.B13C035S01H01: Bhishma says Brahmanas deserve worship by birth and recites Brahma's verses on their duties, their study and sacrifice, their power, and the need for kings to serve them.
shots.B13C035S01H02: A note says the Anusasana Parva continues in Volume XI.
shots.B13C035S01H03: A heading marks the start of Section XXXVI.

B13C036.summary: Bhishma tells of Sakra (Indra), who visits the Asura Samvara in disguise and asks how he rose above his kin. Samvara credits his respect for Brahmanas and his willingness to learn from them, and he repeats what his father heard from Soma about the power of Brahmanas. Sakra then takes up the same devotion to Brahmanas and gains the chiefdom of the gods. The story is offered as an example of honouring Brahmanas.

scenes.B13C036S01: Sakra's disguised visit to Samvara, Samvara's account of his devotion to Brahmanas and Soma's teaching, and Sakra's rise after taking up the same course.

shots.B13C036S01H01: Bhishma introduces the story: Sakra, disguised as a matted-haired ascetic, visits the Asura Samvara in a plain car.
shots.B13C036S01H02: Sakra asks Samvara how he won leadership over his people.
shots.B13C036S01H03: Samvara says he respects Brahmanas, learns from them, serves them and takes their teaching to heart; he compares them to bees filling honeycomb.
shots.B13C036S01H04: Samvara repeats Soma's teaching to his father: Brahmanas gain success through penance and speech, should study the Vedas, and should not stay idle at home.
shots.B13C036S01H05: Bhishma says Sakra was moved by these words, began to honour Brahmanas, and gained the chiefdom of the gods.

B13C037.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether a stranger, a long-known companion, or a traveller from afar is the best recipient of a gift. Bhishma says all three can be worthy and lists the qualities that make a recipient deserving, such as learning, truthfulness and self-restraint. He condemns quarrelsome and vain Brahmanas and sets out the householder's duties to the gods, sages, ancestors, Brahmanas and guests. The chapter teaches that the worth of the person matters more than how well one knows them.

scenes.B13C037S01: Yudhishthira's question on the choice of recipients, Bhishma's answer on worthiness, and the householder's duties to others.

shots.B13C037S01H01: Yudhishthira asks which kind of person is the best recipient of a gift: a stranger, a long-known companion, or a visitor from far away.
shots.B13C037S01H02: Bhishma says all three are equal in claim, that gifts should not harm one's dependants, and that a newcomer, a familiar person and a distant traveller all deserve gifts.
shots.B13C037S01H03: Yudhishthira agrees that gifts must not break the scriptures, and says the giver must first judge whether the gift will benefit the recipient.
shots.B13C037S01H04: Bhishma lists the qualities of a worthy recipient, condemns quarrelsome and proud Brahmanas, and sets out the householder's duties to the gods, sages, ancestors, Brahmanas and guests.

B13C038.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to describe the nature of women, whom he calls the root of evil. Bhishma tells of Narada questioning the Apsara Panchachuda, who at first refuses to speak ill of her own sex and then does so at Narada's urging. She lists the faults she ascribes to women, including restlessness, a readiness to break restraints, and an inability to be satisfied. The chapter presents these as a view attributed to Panchachuda, and it sets up the next chapter's question about men and women.

scenes.B13C038S01: Yudhishthira's request, Narada's meeting with Panchachuda, and her agreement to answer.
scenes.B13C038S02: Panchachuda's account of the faults she ascribes to women.

shots.B13C038S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to speak about the nature of women, whom he calls the root of evil and very frail.
shots.B13C038S01H02: Bhishma introduces an old story in which Narada meets the Apsara Panchachuda in Brahma's realm and asks her a question.
shots.B13C038S01H03: Panchachuda says she will answer if the subject is within her knowledge.
shots.B13C038S01H04: Narada asks her to explain the disposition of women.
shots.B13C038S01H05: Panchachuda says she cannot speak ill of her own sex, Narada says that speaking the truth is no fault, and she agrees to answer.
shots.B13C038S02H01: Panchachuda lists the faults she attributes to women: they break their restraints, favour any man who courts them, are never satisfied, and were created with these faults.

B13C039.summary: Yudhishthira presses Bhishma with doubts raised by the previous account: why men still attach themselves to women despite their faults, whether women can deceive and sway men, and whether anyone has ever restrained them. He asks Bhishma to explain how men can protect women and whether women can truly be kept within the bounds set by the scriptures.

scenes.B13C039S01: Yudhishthira's series of questions on why men are drawn to women, whether women can be restrained, and whether anyone has managed it.

shots.B13C039S01H01: Yudhishthira asks why men are drawn to women despite their faults, how women are said to deceive men, whether women can be restrained, and whether anyone has ever succeeded in restraining them.

B13C040.summary: Bhishma says women were created by Brahma after the gods feared that humans would become too righteous, and that they were given desire and anger. He then tells how the sage Devasarman, about to leave for a sacrifice, asks his disciple Vipula to guard his wife Ruchi from Indra. Devasarman describes Indra's endless disguises, and Vipula enters Ruchi's body by yoga power so that Indra cannot approach her. The chapter sets up the test of Vipula's devotion.

scenes.B13C040S01: The account of how women were created, and Devasarman's instruction to Vipula to protect his wife Ruchi from Indra.
scenes.B13C040S02: Devasarman's description of Indra's disguises and Vipula's decision to enter Ruchi's body to guard her.

shots.B13C040S01H01: Bhishma says women are sinful and recounts how Brahma created them after the gods feared human righteousness; then he introduces the story of Vipula guarding the wife of his teacher, Devasarman.
shots.B13C040S01H02: Devasarman says he is leaving for a sacrifice, warns that Indra covets his wife Ruchi, and asks Vipula to guard her closely.
shots.B13C040S01H03: Vipula agrees to do so, but as his teacher is about to leave he asks one more question.
shots.B13C040S01H04: Vipula asks what forms Indra takes and what his body and power are like.
shots.B13C040S01H05: Bhishma says the sage Devasarman truly described all of Indra's illusions to Vipula.
shots.B13C040S02H01: Devasarman describes Indra's many shapes; Vipula weighs the options and decides to enter Ruchi's body by yoga power, staying unseen to guard her until his teacher returns.

B13C041.summary: Indra comes to the hermitage in a beautiful form, intending to seduce Ruchi, but finds that Vipula has bound her body and speech from inside. Indra speaks to her, and she is forced to say words Vipula controls, while Vipula watches Indra's approach from within her. When Vipula reveals himself and rebukes Indra, mentioning Gautama's curse, Indra flees in shame. Devasarman rewards Vipula with a boon that he will never fall from righteousness.

scenes.B13C041S01: Indra's visit to the hermitage, Vipula's rebuke of Indra, and Devasarman's reward to his disciple.

shots.B13C041S01H01: Indra takes a beautiful form and enters the hermitage; Vipula sits motionless inside Ruchi, who cannot rise to welcome him, and Indra speaks to her while Vipula controls her words; Indra is shamed, sees Vipula, and fears his curse.
shots.B13C041S01H02: Vipula comes out of Ruchi's body and rebukes Indra, recalls Gautama's curse that gave him his sex-marks, and warns him to respect the Brahmanas and leave.
shots.B13C041S01H03: Indra slips away in shame; Devasarman returns, hears Vipula's account, praises him, and grants him a boon that he will never fall from righteousness.

B13C042.summary: Vipula, after his success, grows proud of his penance. When Devasarman's sister-in-law asks for celestial flowers, Vipula is sent to fetch some and finds them where Ruchi had dropped them. On the road he hears two couples swear oaths naming his fate in the next world, and he searches his conscience and recalls that he never told his teacher about entering Ruchi's body. He then brings the flowers and honours his teacher. The chapter shows that even a just act can leave a hidden fault.

scenes.B13C042S01: Vipula's pride after his penance, the errand for flowers, the oaths overheard on the road, and his realisation of his own fault.

shots.B13C042S01H01: Vipula, proud of his penance, is sent by his teacher to fetch the same flowers that Ruchi's sister wants; he finds them, passes two quarrelling couples and a group of dice players who each swear oaths naming his fate, and at last recalls that he never told his teacher about entering Ruchi's body; he delivers the flowers and honours his teacher.

B13C043.summary: Devasarman greets his returning disciple Vipula and explains that the two couples and the dice players were Day and Night and the six Seasons, who see every hidden deed. Vipula had not told his teacher the whole truth, but Devasarman judges that his protection of Ruchi was proper and sends him to heaven. Bhishma then recounts a lesson he had from the sage Markandeya: women must be guarded, virtuous women are blessed, and men should not become overly attached to them. Only Vipula is said to have protected women successfully.

scenes.B13C043S01: Devasarman's welcome of Vipula, his explanation of the witnesses to Vipula's fault, and the closing lesson Bhishma draws about women.

shots.B13C043S01H01: Bhishma says Devasarman addressed his disciple Vipula on his return from the errand.
shots.B13C043S01H02: Devasarman says he knows how Vipula protected Ruchi, and asks what Vipula saw on his journey.
shots.B13C043S01H03: Vipula asks who the two couples and six men were, since they seemed to know him.
shots.B13C043S01H04: Devasarman explains that they were Day and Night and the six Seasons, who witness every deed; he says Vipula's concealment was a fault, but his protection of Ruchi was proper, so he sends him to heaven. Bhishma adds that he heard this from Markandeya, and that women should be guarded, virtuous women are blessed, men should not be over-attached, and only Vipula protected women.

B13C044.summary: Yudhishthira asks how a father should choose a husband for his daughter, and Bhishma answers at length on marriage. He names the several forms of marriage, separates the righteous forms from the unrighteous, and sets rules on how many wives each caste may take, on suitable ages and on whom a girl may not marry. Yudhishthira then asks whether a dowry alone makes a bride a wife, and Bhishma answers that only the rites of marriage do, recalling his own seizure of maidens for Vichitravirya. The chapter's main point is that the taking of the hand with proper rites creates the marriage.

scenes.B13C044S01: Yudhishthira's question on choosing a bridegroom, Bhishma's account of marriage forms and rules, and Yudhishthira's question about dower and promises.
scenes.B13C044S02: Yudhishthira's question about a rejected dowry suitor, and Bhishma's answer on dower, sale, and the rites that make a marriage.

shots.B13C044S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma whom a father should choose as a husband for his daughter, calling marriage the foremost duty.
shots.B13C044S01H02: Bhishma says the father should judge the groom's conduct, learning and birth before giving his daughter, and describes the Brahma and Gandharva forms of marriage and the Asura form of purchase.
shots.B13C044S01H03: Bhishma describes the Rakshasa form, calls three of the five forms righteous and two not, gives the number of wives each caste may take, and sets rules on marriage ages, unmarried girls, and whom one may not wed.
shots.B13C044S01H04: Yudhishthira asks whose wife the girl becomes when a dower is paid, promised, or simply displayed, or when a suitor takes her hand with rites.
shots.B13C044S01H05: Bhishma says the girl's hand must be given with proper rites and the kinsmen's consent, that a marriage forced on an unwilling girl brings sin, and that a girl promised to another does not make a later marriage wrong.
shots.B13C044S02H01: Yudhishthira asks how a father should act when a more eligible suitor appears after a dower has been accepted from another.
shots.B13C044S02H02: Bhishma says a dower does not make a girl a wife, that such a payment is a price rather than a marriage, and that a promise or a father's declaration is not marriage either.
shots.B13C044S02H03: Bhishma recounts how he seized two maidens for Vichitravirya, and how king Valhika ruled that a wife is made by the proper giving and taking of her hand, not by a sale. Prince Satyavat then answers questions on a dower-giver who dies, a widow's remarriage to a brother-in-law, and the wedding rites that end at the seventh step, concluding with the gift of a maiden with water and the circling of the fire.

B13C045.summary: Yudhishthira asks what should happen when a dowry-giver walks away from a marriage, and Bhishma answers with a set of rules on the girl's maintenance and on the rights of daughters and their sons. He cites the case of Savitri and an opinion of a king of Videha's line, and says a woman is never free. He then argues that a daughter sold for a price, or a dower taken for a daughter, is a sinful sale, and recites Yama's warning of punishment in hell for those who sell their children. The chapter treats marriage by sale as wrong.

scenes.B13C045S01: Yudhishthira's question on a jilted dowry-giver, Bhishma's rules on maintenance and inheritance by daughters and their sons, and his condemnation of sale in marriage.

shots.B13C045S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what the father or kinsmen should do when a man who gave a dowry walks away from the marriage.
shots.B13C045S01H02: Bhishma says the girl should be maintained by her father, and that the dowry-giver may claim her, but may not marry her by proper rites; he cites Savitri's choice of a husband and an opinion of a king of Videha's line that women are never free.
shots.B13C045S01H03: Yudhishthira asks on what authority a man's wealth passes to others when he has only daughters.
shots.B13C045S01H04: Bhishma says a daughter is like a son, and explains inheritance rules for daughters and daughters' sons, including the case where a sold daughter's sons belong to the buyer. He cites Yama's verse on the hell awaiting those who sell children, condemns the Arsha and forced marriages as sale or sin, and says no wealth gained by sin can buy merit.

B13C046.summary: Bhishma says a maiden for whom no dowry has been taken is not sold, and that a wife should be respected and kindly treated, since a family's prosperity depends on how its women are treated. He recalls Manu's instruction that men must protect and honour women, and he quotes a verse of a princess of Videha's house on a woman's duty to serve her husband and her lifelong need for protection. The chapter closes by saying that honouring women is honouring prosperity itself.

scenes.B13C046S01: Bhishma's verses on dowry and sale, his teaching on respect for wives, and the verse on women's duty and protection.

shots.B13C046S01H01: Bhishma recites Daksha's view that a maiden for whom no dowry is taken is not sold, then urges respect and kindness towards wives, warns that a family whose women suffer will decline, and cites Manu's charge to men to protect women.

B13C047.summary: Yudhishthira asks how a Brahmana's sons from different wives should divide his property, since a Brahmana may take wives from all four classes. Bhishma sets out the shares: out of ten parts, the son of the Brahmana wife takes four, the Kshatriya wife's son three, the Vaisya wife's son two, and the Sudra wife's son one part only if his father gives it. Yudhishthira objects that all the sons are Brahmanas by birth, and Bhishma answers that the Brahmana wife ranks first and that Kshatriyas, who protect society, are rightly given a larger share than Vaisyas. Yudhishthira then asks about the rules for other classes, and Bhishma gives the Kshatriya and Vaisya rules and the law for the eldest son, which Kasyapa is said to have declared.

scenes.B13C047S01: Yudhishthira's question on inheritance among a Brahmana's sons, Bhishma's shares for the Brahmana's sons, Yudhishthira's objection, and Bhishma's reasons for ranking the wives.
scenes.B13C047S02: Yudhishthira asks about other classes, and Bhishma gives the Kshatriya and Vaisya rules and the rule of the eldest son.

shots.B13C047S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how the property of a Brahmana with wives from four classes should pass to his sons.
shots.B13C047S01H02: Bhishma says a Brahmana should marry within the three higher classes, and that a Sudra wife brings sin and expiation; he then divides the Brahmana's property into ten parts, four to the Brahmana wife's son, three to the Kshatriya's, two to the Vaisya's and one to the Sudra's, only if the father gives it; he adds rules on a wife's own allowance and the daughter's share.
shots.B13C047S01H03: Yudhishthira asks why the Sudra-born son should get any share at all, since all the sons are Brahmanas by birth.
shots.B13C047S01H04: Bhishma says all wives are called Data, but the Brahmana wife ranks highest; he explains that Brahmanas and Kshatriyas each have a proper rank, and that the Kshatriya's son takes a larger share than the Vaisya's because Kshatriyas protect society.
shots.B13C047S01H05: Yudhishthira says Bhishma has explained the rules for Brahmanas.
shots.B13C047S02H01: Yudhishthira asks what rules apply to the other classes.
shots.B13C047S02H02: Bhishma gives the rules for Kshatriyas (two wives, eight shares) and Vaisyas (one wife, five shares), says the Sudra may have only one wife, and states that the eldest son takes one extra share, a rule Kasyapa declared.

B13C048.summary: Yudhishthira asks what duties fall to people born of mixed unions between the four classes. Bhishma explains that the four classes were set up for sacrifice, and then lists the offspring of each mixed pairing, such as the Suta, Magadha, Chandala and Nishada, with the work each is assigned. He warns that such unions multiply lower castes and bring grief to the father. Yudhishthira then asks how a man of mixed birth can be recognised, and the chapter ends with the warning that men of wisdom should not become overly attached to women.

scenes.B13C048S01: Yudhishthira's question on mixed-class duties, Bhishma's list of mixed-class offspring and their occupations, and Yudhishthira's question on how to recognise mixed birth.

shots.B13C048S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what duties fall to those born of mixed classes, through lust, greed or ignorance of birth.
shots.B13C048S01H02: Bhishma says the four orders were set up for sacrifice, explains the status and duties of the offspring of each mixed pairing, such as the Parasara, Ugra, Suta, Vaidehaka, Chandala, Magadha and Nishada, and their multiplication into many lower castes; he warns that lust and women's pull lead men astray, so wise men avoid excessive attachment.
shots.B13C048S01H03: Yudhishthira asks whether there are signs by which a person of impure birth, who looks respectable, can be recognised.

B13C049.summary: Bhishma says a person's birth shows in his conduct, since a son takes after his parents and cannot hide his origin for long. Yudhishthira asks for the kinds of sons recognised by law, and Bhishma lists the sons born of wives, of outsiders, and of mixed unions. A debate follows over whether the seed or the soil makes a son, and Bhishma rules that the soil-owner's son belongs to him, and that a found and raised child becomes the rearer's son. The chapter ends with the purification rites for such children.

scenes.B13C049S01: Bhishma on how birth shows in conduct, and his list of the kinds of sons and of the sons of mixed unions.
scenes.B13C049S02: Yudhishthira's debate on seed versus soil in determining sonship, and Bhishma's ruling on abandoned and made sons.
scenes.B13C049S03: Bhishma on the foundling who is raised by a rearer, and the purification rites for such children.

shots.B13C049S01H01: Bhishma says birth shows in conduct, that a son takes after his sire or his mother, and that goodness of understanding only counts when it matches the person's order; he advises avoiding women with whom offspring would be improper.
shots.B13C049S01H02: Yudhishthira asks for teaching on the orders, the sons of different wives, and the disputes that arise over sons.
shots.B13C049S01H03: Bhishma lists the kinds of sons: a son of one's loins, a son begotten by an invited man, a son begotten without consent, a son of a fallen man, the given, the made, the Adhyudha, and the Kanina, as well as the six Apadhwansajas and six Apasadas.
shots.B13C049S01H04: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to explain the Apadhwansajas and the Apasadas.
shots.B13C049S01H05: Bhishma explains the Apadhwansajas (sons of a Brahmana, Kshatriya or Vaisya by lower wives) and the Apasadas (Chandala, Vratya, Vaidya, Magadha, Vamaka and Suta), and says all six are sons.
shots.B13C049S02H01: Yudhishthira asks whether the son belongs to the one who owns the soil or to the one who gave the seed, and whether both are equal.
shots.B13C049S02H02: Bhishma says a son belongs to the seed-giver, unless the seed-giver abandons him, in which case he belongs to his mother's husband; the same goes for the Adhyudha.
shots.B13C049S02H03: Yudhishthira asks how the mother's husband can own a son when the seed-giver made the child.
shots.B13C049S02H04: Bhishma says the seed alone does not make a son, that a child born in the soil of a man who married a pregnant woman belongs to the soil-owner, and that the made son is the one who has been adopted and brought up.
shots.B13C049S02H05: Yudhishthira asks what kind of son the made son is, whose sonship rests on rearing rather than seed or soil.
shots.B13C049S03H01: Bhishma says a child abandoned by his parents and raised by a finder, who cannot trace the parents, becomes the rearer's made son and takes the rearer's order.
shots.B13C049S03H02: Yudhishthira asks what purification rites apply to such a son and whom he should marry.
shots.B13C049S03H03: Bhishma says the purification rites follow the rearer's custom and kin, and that children of unwed or pre-marriage birth receive the same rites as other sons; he ends by asking whether Yudhishthira wants more.

B13C050.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about compassion, the bonds formed by living together, and the blessedness of cows. Bhishma begins a story about the sage Chyavana, who takes a vow to stand still in the water at the Ganga and Yamuna confluence for a long time. A group of fishermen nets him along with a heap of fish, and he refuses to be parted from the fish. The fishermen, terrified, report to king Nahusha. The chapter sets up the story's test of compassion and devotion.

scenes.B13C050S01: Yudhishthira's questions, Chyavana's vow in the river, the fishermen's catch, and Chyavana's refusal to leave the fish.

shots.B13C050S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about compassion at another's suffering, the bonds that come from living together, and the blessedness of cows.
shots.B13C050S01H02: Bhishma introduces the story of Nahusha and the sage Chyavana, who takes a twelve-year vow and stands in the river like a post while the current rushes past him.
shots.B13C050S01H03: A group of fishermen cast a large net, drag Chyavana up with the fish, and bow to him; the fish die, and Chyavana is moved to pity. The fishermen apologise and offer to do whatever he wishes.
shots.B13C050S01H04: Chyavana says he will either die with the fish or be sold with them, and does not want to abandon them; the fishermen go in fear to report to king Nahusha.

B13C051.summary: King Nahusha comes to the river and offers Chyavana ever larger sums to free him: a thousand coins, a hundred thousand, a crore, and finally half his kingdom. Chyavana rejects each offer and tells Nahusha to consult the Brahmanas. A sage born of a cow proposes a cow as the price, since Brahmanas are beyond price, and Chyavana praises cows as the source of sacrifice, prosperity and heaven. The fishermen, moved by Chyavana, return the cow, and Chyavana sends them and the fish to heaven. Both sages grant Nahusha boons before he returns to his city.

scenes.B13C051S01: Nahusha's arrival and his first offer of a thousand coins, which Chyavana refuses.
scenes.B13C051S02: Nahusha's offers of a hundred thousand coins and then a crore, both refused.
scenes.B13C051S03: Nahusha's offer of half his kingdom, its refusal, and the cow-born sage's proposal that a cow is the price.
scenes.B13C051S04: Nahusha accepts the cow as the price, Chyavana praises cows, and the fishermen offer to return the cow, which Chyavana accepts while freeing them.
scenes.B13C051S05: The fishermen and the fish ascend to heaven, the sages grant Nahusha boons, and Nahusha returns to his city, and Bhishma ends by listing the topics he has covered.

shots.B13C051S01H01: Bhishma says Nahusha hears of Chyavana's plight, goes to the spot with his ministers and priest, and honours the sage.
shots.B13C051S01H02: Nahusha asks Chyavana what he should do, promising to accomplish anything.
shots.B13C051S01H03: Chyavana asks Nahusha to pay the fishermen the price of himself and the fish.
shots.B13C051S01H04: Nahusha orders his priest to give the fishermen a thousand coins for the sage.
shots.B13C051S01H05: Chyavana says a thousand coins cannot be his price and asks Nahusha to set a fair value.
shots.B13C051S02H01: Nahusha offers a hundred thousand coins and asks if that is enough.
shots.B13C051S02H02: Chyavana refuses that sum and asks Nahusha to consult his ministers about a fair price.
shots.B13C051S02H03: Nahusha orders his priest to give the fishermen a crore of coins.
shots.B13C051S02H04: Nahusha adds that more should be paid if a crore is not enough.
shots.B13C051S02H05: Chyavana refuses even a crore and asks Nahusha to consult the Brahmanas.
shots.B13C051S03H01: Nahusha offers half of his kingdom, or all of it, as the price.
shots.B13C051S03H02: Chyavana refuses the kingdom and asks Nahusha to consult the sages.
shots.B13C051S03H03: Nahusha is grieved and deliberates with his advisers; a sage born of a cow arrives and promises to satisfy both the king and Chyavana.
shots.B13C051S03H04: Nahusha begs the cow-born sage to name the price, since Chyavana's anger could destroy the three worlds.
shots.B13C051S03H05: The cow-born sage says Brahmanas have no price and cows are priceless, so a cow should be the price; Nahusha is glad.
shots.B13C051S04H01: Nahusha tells Chyavana that he has been bought for a cow, which is his proper price.
shots.B13C051S04H02: Chyavana accepts and praises cows at length as the source of sacrifice, prosperity and heaven.
shots.B13C051S04H03: Bhishma says he can only describe part of the glory of cows.
shots.B13C051S04H04: The fishermen beg Chyavana's grace and offer to take back the cow.
shots.B13C051S04H05: Chyavana accepts the cow back and tells the fishermen to go to heaven with their catch.
shots.B13C051S05H01: The fishermen and fish ascend to heaven; Nahusha is amazed; the two sages grant him boons, and Chyavana returns to his hermitage. Bhishma closes by listing the topics of compassion, companionship, the blessings of cows, and true righteousness, and asks Yudhishthira what else he wants to know.

B13C052.summary: Yudhishthira asks why Rama, the son of Jamadagni, a Brahmana by birth, took up Kshatriya ways, and how a Kshatriya son of Kusika became a Brahmana. Bhishma tells how Chyavana, foreseeing that his own race would be stained by Kshatriya practice through a Kusika descendant, decides to bring ruin on the Kusika line. He asks king Kusika to let him stay, and the king and queen serve him for twenty-one days without food. When the sage finally leaves unseen, the king is left in grief, searching for him.

scenes.B13C052S01: Yudhishthira's questions on Rama and the Kusika line, Chyavana's plan, Kusika's welcome, and the king's service to the sage until the sage vanishes.

shots.B13C052S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how Rama, born into a Brahmana family, came to follow Kshatriya ways, and how a Kshatriya son of Kusika became a Brahmana; he also asks why the grandsons, rather than the sons, of Richika and Kusika took opposite paths.
shots.B13C052S01H02: Bhishma tells of Chyavana, who sees that his own race will be stained by a Kusika descendant's Kshatriya ways, and decides to bring ruin on the Kusika line; he asks King Kusika to let him stay.
shots.B13C052S01H03: Kusika says living with a guest is not an ordained custom, but he agrees to do whatever the sage asks.
shots.B13C052S01H04: Kusika and his queen honour Chyavana with water, food and every courtesy, and offer their wealth, kingdom and throne.
shots.B13C052S01H05: Chyavana declines the riches and asks the king and queen to serve him during a vow; they wait on him through twenty-one days and nights without food while he sleeps, then he leaves unseen and the stricken king searches for him.

B13C053.summary: After Chyavana vanishes, king Kusika and his queen keep serving him. He returns repeatedly, burns the food they prepare, and then makes the royal couple yoke themselves to a battle-car and drag him about, goading them until they bleed. Through all of it they show no anger, and Chyavana finally heals their wounds, gives away treasure, and sends them home young and beautiful again. The chapter shows the sage testing the king's patience, which the king passes.

scenes.B13C053S01: Yudhishthira's question, Kusika's repeated service to Chyavana, the burnt food, the goading in the battle-car, Chyavana's gifts and healing, and the transformed riverbank.

shots.B13C053S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what Kusika and his queen did after Chyavana disappeared.
shots.B13C053S01H02: Kusika returns home in grief, then finds Chyavana asleep on his bed again; the couple resume serving him, bathe him in oil, and prepare a lavish feast, which Chyavana sets on fire; the sage then sets the king and queen to yoke themselves to a battle-car and drives them through the city, goading them until they bleed, while they show no anger.
shots.B13C053S01H03: Chyavana gives away the royal treasure, then heals the couple with a touch, and tells Kusika he has passed the test and may return to the city; Kusika and his queen go home youthful and beautiful, and Chyavana turns the riverbank into a splendid retreat.

B13C054.summary: Kusika goes back to the wood and sees a golden palace, celestial trees and musicians, which vanish when he tries to approach. He realises that Chyavana has shown him these marvels by his yoga power and that penance is superior even to sovereignty. Chyavana, satisfied that the king has come through the ordeal without sin, offers him a boon. Kusika's reply sets the stage for his questions to the sage.

scenes.B13C054S01: Kusika's visit to the golden palace and its disappearance, Chyavana's praise of the king, and Kusika's reply.

shots.B13C054S01H01: Kusika goes to the wood and sees a golden palace, wondrous trees, birds and musicians; the scene vanishes when Chyavana is approached, and the king reflects on the power of penance and the status of Brahmanas. Chyavana tells the king he has passed the fiery test and offers a boon.
shots.B13C054S01H02: Kusika says that surviving the ordeal and pleasing the sage are boon enough, and asks the sage to answer some doubts he has.

B13C055.summary: Chyavana offers Kusika a boon and asks him to state his doubts. Kusika asks why the sage put him through his long trials, the feast he burned, the car, the gifts, and the vanishing palace. Chyavana explains that he came to destroy Kusika's race because the gods foretold a clash of Brahmana and Kshatriya energy in it, but he found the king blameless. He then tested the king to show the rewards of penance and promised that a descendant of Kusika would become a Brahmana. Kusika asks for the details of how this will happen.

scenes.B13C055S01: Chyavana's offer, Kusika's list of questions, Chyavana's explanation of his trials, and Kusika's request for details of the Brahmana descent.

shots.B13C055S01H01: Chyavana offers Kusika a boon and asks him to name his doubt.
shots.B13C055S01H02: Kusika asks why Chyavana slept, went out in silence, vanished, burned the food, drove the car, gave away wealth, and showed the golden wonders, and why they vanished.
shots.B13C055S01H03: Chyavana says the Creator foretold a clash of Brahmana and Kshatriya energy, so he came to destroy Kusika's race; finding the king blameless, he tested him to show the rewards of penance, and he promises that a grandson will become a Brahmana and an ascetic of great fire, and that a descendant in the third generation will gain Brahmana status.
shots.B13C055S01H04: Kusika says this is a high boon, asks that his race attain Brahmanahood, and asks how this will come about and who will be his kin and friends.

B13C056.summary: Chyavana explains the wider pattern. The Kshatriyas and the Bhargavas will fall out, and the Kshatriyas will destroy the Bhrigu line until a sage named Urva rises with fury that he cools in the sea. Urva's line leads to Jamadagni, who marries Kusika's granddaughter, and their son Viswamitra is born a Kshatriya. Richika then gives a Brahmana son to Kusika's line in exchange, so the two lines are joined by marriage. Kusika accepts the promise, and Bhishma says the events of Rama and Viswamitra came about as Chyavana foretold.

scenes.B13C056S01: Chyavana's prophecy of the Bhargava-Kshatriya conflict and the marriage and exchange of sons that link the two families, and Bhishma's closing confirmation.

shots.B13C056S01H01: Chyavana foretells the Kshatriya-Bhargava conflict, the rise of Urva and Richika, Jamadagni's marriage to Gadhi's daughter, the birth of Viswamitra as a Kshatriya, and the exchange of sons that makes Kusika's third descendant a Brahmana.
shots.B13C056S01H02: Kusika accepts the promise and asks for his race to attain Brahmana status; Chyavana grants it and leaves, and Bhishma says the births of Rama and Viswamitra happened as foretold.

B13C057.summary: Yudhishthira is overwhelmed by the deaths of many kings and kinsmen in the war and says he wants to undertake severe penance. Vaisampayana then introduces Bhishma's reply, in which Bhishma lists the rewards that different acts of penance, austerity, vows, and gifts bring in the next life. He especially praises gifts of cows, land, houses and other goods to Brahmanas. Yudhishthira, moved by the account, sets aside his disgust at the householder's life, and the brothers agree to follow the grandsire's words.

scenes.B13C057S01: Yudhishthira's grief over the war, Bhishma's long account of the rewards of penance and gifts, and the brothers' acceptance of the grandsire's words.

shots.B13C057S01H01: Yudhishthira grieves over the millions slain in the war and the widows left behind, believing the Kurus he killed will send him to hell, and asks Bhishma for instruction in penance.
shots.B13C057S01H02: The narrator Vaisampayana says Bhishma reflected on Yudhishthira's words and prepared to answer.
shots.B13C057S01H03: Bhishma lists the rewards that various acts bring after death, such as heaven, fame and wealth from penances and vows, and especially from gifts of cows, land, houses, food, lamps, garments, and other goods to Brahmanas.
shots.B13C057S01H04: Vaisampayana reports that Yudhishthira is moved to seek the end reserved for heroes and no longer despises the householder's life; he asks the brothers to accept the grandsire's words, and they all agree.

B13C058.summary: Yudhishthira asks what rewards come from planting trees and digging tanks. Bhishma says a tank brings a man honour in the three worlds and that water in a tank in each season counts as a particular sacrifice, with water given to kine and other creatures counting most. He says gifts of water are the highest of gifts and that planting trees brings fame, honour among the Pitris, and rescue for one's ancestors. The chapter urges making tanks, planting trees, sacrificing and speaking the truth.

scenes.B13C058S01: Yudhishthira's question, and Bhishma's account of the merit of tanks and of tree planting.

shots.B13C058S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what rewards come from planting trees and digging tanks.
shots.B13C058S01H02: Bhishma says a tank earns honour, that its water counts as sacrifices by season, that gifts of water are the foremost gifts, and that planting trees brings fame and rescues ancestors; he ends by urging tanks, trees, sacrifice and truth.

B13C059.summary: Yudhishthira asks which gift is best among those not found in the Vedas, and which follows the giver after death. Bhishma says the best gifts are kindness, relief for the distressed, and gifts given without pride; gifts of gold, cows and land cleanse sin. He urges giving to worthy, learned Brahmanas, especially those who do not ask, and calls such giving a sacrifice. He ends by insisting that kings must honour Brahmanas, since kingly power yields to them, and he says he loves them above all.

scenes.B13C059S01: Yudhishthira's question on the best gift, and Bhishma's long answer on giving, the merit of Brahmanas, and the duty of kings to them.

shots.B13C059S01H01: Yudhishthira asks which gift is most distinguished and which one follows the giver into the next world.
shots.B13C059S01H02: Bhishma calls kindness, relief for the distressed, and gifts given without vanity the highest gifts; he praises gifts of gold, cows and land, urges generosity to the poor and worthy, and says that kings must honour Brahmanas, whose disciplined lives make giving to them a sacrifice; he closes by declaring that the Brahmanas are dearer to him than anyone.

B13C060.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether a gift is more meritorious when given to a Brahmana who asks or to one who does not, if they are otherwise equal. Bhishma says a gift to one who does not ask earns more merit, since a Brahmana's firmness lies in not begging. He says begging brings shame and that the giver is said to grant life to the one who asks. Bhishma urges kings to seek out such contented Brahmanas, invite them, and feed and honour them, calling this a sacrifice that pleases the gods.

scenes.B13C060S01: Yudhishthira's question on gifts to a begging versus a non-begging Brahmana, and Bhishma's answer on contentment and the worth of gifts to the unasking.

shots.B13C060S01H01: Yudhishthira asks which of two equally qualified Brahmanas deserves a gift more, the one who begs or the one who does not.
shots.B13C060S01H02: Bhishma says a gift to one who does not ask earns greater merit, that a Brahmana's firmness lies in not begging, that begging is a reproach, and that kings should seek out and honour such Brahmanas with houses, food and other gifts, as a kind of sacrifice.

B13C061.summary: Yudhishthira asks where the rewards of gifts and sacrifices are earned, which is greater, and who should receive gifts. Bhishma says a king should give to righteous Brahmanas, support them with food, cattle and dwellings, and protect their means of living, and that such giving benefits a king more than grand sacrifices. He warns that a king who extorts wealth gains no merit from the sacrifices it pays for, and that a king who fails to protect his people, or lets learned Brahmanas go hungry, bears a share of their sins. The chapter ends by urging Yudhishthira to be a protector his subjects will trust.

scenes.B13C061S01: Yudhishthira's questions on gifts and sacrifices, Bhishma's advice on royal giving, and his warnings about the king's duty to protect his people.

shots.B13C061S01H01: Yudhishthira asks where the rewards of gifts and sacrifices are earned, which is greater, to whom gifts should go, and how and when they should be made.
shots.B13C061S01H02: Bhishma says a Kshatriya's sacrifices and gifts purify him, that kings should support worthy Brahmanas with cattle, food, homes and goods, and that such giving outweighs royal sacrifices; he warns that wealth extorted from subjects spoils a sacrifice, that a king must protect the weak and the hungry, that the king bears a share of his subjects' sins if he fails to do so, and that subjects may rise against a king who plunders them.

B13C062.summary: Yudhishthira asks which gift is the foremost of all, and Bhishma answers that the gift of earth is the highest, since land lasts and brings wealth to its giver. He says a king should give land to learned Brahmanas, that taking land from the righteous is a grave sin, and that the gift of earth cleanses even great sinners. Bhishma then tells how Indra asked Vrihaspati which gift leads to heaven, and Vrihaspati gave the same answer, that the gift of earth is supreme. The chapter closes with Indra giving the whole earth to Vrihaspati and with advice to recite these verses at funeral rites.

scenes.B13C062S01: Yudhishthira's question, Bhishma's praise of the gift of earth, the exchange between Indra and Vrihaspati, and the closing advice on reciting the verses.

shots.B13C062S01H01: Yudhishthira asks which gift is the best or foremost of all, since kings make many gifts to many men.
shots.B13C062S01H02: Bhishma says the gift of earth is the first and highest, since land lasts and yields wealth to its owner; he explains that giving land cleanses sinners, that a king should give land to learned Brahmanas, that taking land from the righteous is a grave sin, and recites the verse by which Rama gave the whole earth to Kasyapa.
shots.B13C062S01H03: Indra asks the teacher Vrihaspati which gift leads to heaven and to lasting merit.
shots.B13C062S01H04: Vrihaspati replies that a gift of earth to the worthy brings merit beyond great sacrifices, that taking back a gift of earth is punished, that giving land to Brahmanas rescues one's ancestors, and that earth-gifts bring heavenly rewards.
shots.B13C062S01H05: Bhishma says Indra then gave the whole earth to Vrihaspati, and advises reciting these verses at funeral rites, so that the offerings are not seized by demons; he closes by asking whether Yudhishthira wants to hear more.

B13C063.summary: Yudhishthira asks what gifts bring a king immediate gratification from the Brahmanas and lasting rewards. Bhishma says he once put the same question to the sage Narada, who answered that food is the foremost of gifts, since all life and every rite depends on it. Narada urges giving food to Brahmanas, guests and anyone in need, and describes the heavenly mansions earned by such giving. The chapter ends with a heading that marks the start of Section LXIV.

scenes.B13C063S01: Yudhishthira's question, Bhishma's recollection of Narada's teaching on food-gifts, and Narada's account of the heavenly rewards, with a closing heading.

shots.B13C063S01H01: Yudhishthira asks which gifts a king should make to accomplished Brahmanas, which gifts gratify them at once, and which rewards both here and hereafter.
shots.B13C063S01H02: Bhishma says he once put the same questions to the sage Narada and is about to recite Narada's answer.
shots.B13C063S01H03: Narada says food is the foremost gift, that all life and every rite rests on food, and that gifts of food to Brahmanas, guests, the poor, and even dogs or outcastes bring merit; he describes the cycle of rain and crops that feeds creatures, and the rewards of a feast-giver.
shots.B13C063S01H04: Bhishma says he has always given food on Narada's advice and urges Yudhishthira to do the same, then describes the shining heavenly mansions with their food, rivers of milk and abundant goods that await those who give food.
shots.B13C063S01H05: A heading marks the start of Section LXIV.

B13C064.summary: Yudhishthira asks about gifts tied to the planetary conjunctions and the lunar mansions. Bhishma recalls a discourse in which the sage Narada told Devaki, the mother of Krishna, which gifts to make under which lunar constellations. Each mansion is linked with a particular offering and its reward, such as Payasa under Krittika or a cow under Mrigasiras. Bhishma adds that Devaki later passed the teaching on to her daughters-in-law.

scenes.B13C064S01: Yudhishthira's question, Narada's list of gifts for each lunar constellation as told to Devaki, and Bhishma's note on how the teaching was passed on.

shots.B13C064S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to discuss gifts in relation to the conjunctions of the planets and stars.
shots.B13C064S01H02: Bhishma introduces a discourse in which Narada, visiting Dwaraka, answers Devaki's question about gifts.
shots.B13C064S01H03: Narada lists the gifts for each lunar constellation in turn, from Krittika through Bharani, such as ghee-rich Payasa, venison, cows, gold, cars and cloths, along with the heavenly rewards each brings.
shots.B13C064S01H04: Bhishma says Devaki herself repeated this teaching to her daughters-in-law, the wives of Krishna.

B13C065.summary: Bhishma lists the gifts praised by earlier authorities: Atri on gold, King Harischandra on gold's cleansing power, and Manu on the gift of drink. He explains that digging wells and tanks where cows, Brahmanas and people can drink wins large merit, and that gifts of ghee, firewood, umbrellas and cars bring prosperity, protection and success. The chapter ends with Sandilya's view that a car is the best gift.

scenes.B13C065S01: Bhishma's survey of the gifts praised by Atri, Harischandra, Manu and Sandilya, including wells, ghee, firewood, umbrellas and cars.

shots.B13C065S01H01: Bhishma cites Atri on the value of gold gifts, Harischandra on gold's cleansing and life-lengthening power, and Manu on drink as the best gift; he praises digging wells and tanks, gifts of ghee and firewood, and umbrellas, and ends by citing Sandilya's view that a car is the best gift.

B13C066.summary: Yudhishthira asks about the merit of giving sandals to Brahmanas and of giving sesame, land, cows and food. Bhishma says a sandal-gift protects the feet and brings the merit of a vehicle, and that sesame seeds, made by Brahma as food for the Pitris, purify the giver. He tells how the gods asked Brahma for a piece of earth to hold a sacrifice, and how they then granted a share of their merit to the gift of earth. He goes on to praise gifts of shelter, land, cows (which should not be given to butchers or atheists) and food as the highest acts.

scenes.B13C066S01: Yudhishthira's question on sandals and his request for more on sesame, land, cows and food, followed by Bhishma's praise of sesame and the story of the gods' request for earth.
scenes.B13C066S02: Brahma's grant of earth, the gods' sacrifice, and Bhishma's teaching on gifts of land, shelter, cows and food.

shots.B13C066S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what merit comes from giving sandals to a Brahmana whose feet are scorched by hot sand.
shots.B13C066S01H02: Bhishma says sandals protect the feet, overcome enemies, and bring the merit of gifting a fine vehicle.
shots.B13C066S01H03: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to repeat the merits of gifts of sesame, land, cows and food.
shots.B13C066S01H04: Bhishma says sesame was made by Brahma as food for the Pitris and that gifts of sesame purify the giver; he gives examples of sages who reached heaven by such gifts, and prepares to tell of the gods' request for earth.
shots.B13C066S01H05: The gods ask Brahma for a piece of earth to hold their sacrifice, saying that a sacrifice performed on land not lawfully obtained brings no merit.
shots.B13C066S02H01: Brahma grants the gods a piece of earth on which to hold their sacrifice.
shots.B13C066S02H02: The gods hold their sacrifice on the Himavat mountain with famous sages present, and attach a sixth part of its merit to the gift of earth; Bhishma then praises gifts of a house, shelter, land, mineral-rich land, and kine, and says that Brahma's cows should not be given to butchers, farmers, atheists or herdsmen; he ends by praising the gift of food and the merit of gifts of sesame, earth, and kine.

B13C067.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to describe the merits of giving drink, after hearing that food is the highest gift. Bhishma says food and drink together are unmatched among gifts, since all life depends on food and food depends on water. He describes how nectar, plants and the very sources of life come from water, and says the gift of water brings fame, long life, victory over enemies, and a place in heaven. Manu is cited as the authority.

scenes.B13C067S01: Yudhishthira's question on drink, and Bhishma's account of why water is the highest gift.

shots.B13C067S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to explain the great merits of giving drink, now that he has heard about food.
shots.B13C067S01H02: Bhishma says food and drink together are unmatched as gifts, that all life depends on food, and that everything, including food and nectar, arises from water; he says the gift of water brings long life, fame and victory, and cites Manu's promise of endless heaven.

B13C068.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma again about the merit of gifts of sesame, lamps, food and robes. Bhishma tells the story of Yama, lord of the dead, who sends a messenger to fetch a learned Brahmana named Sarmin, but the messenger brings the wrong man, a Brahmana who wants to finish his life in peace. Yama sends him back and instructs him to give sesame, water and resting places, and to light lamps; Sarmin does so. The chapter goes on to praise lamps, gems, robes and a son as the greatest acquisition.

scenes.B13C068S01: Yudhishthira's question, and Yama's instructions to a Brahmana through the story of a mistaken summons.
scenes.B13C068S02: The Brahmana's return to the world and his practice of the gifts, and Bhishma's closing teaching on lamps, gems, robes and offspring.

shots.B13C068S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to speak again about gifts of sesame, lamps, food and robes.
shots.B13C068S01H02: Bhishma tells the story of Yama sending a messenger to fetch the learned Brahmana Sarmin of Agastya's line from the town of Parnasala; the messenger instead brings another Brahmana, whom Yama honours and wants returned.
shots.B13C068S01H03: Yama says he cannot fix a man's allotted time, so he cannot let the Brahmana stay; he tells him to go home and say what he needs from Yama.
shots.B13C068S01H04: The Brahmana asks Yama what acts bring the greatest merit.
shots.B13C068S01H05: Yama teaches that gifts of sesame are supremely meritorious, that they should be made on certain days and at Sraddhas, that water-gifts and water stations are rare and praiseworthy, and that wells and tanks should be dug.
shots.B13C068S02H01: Bhishma says the messenger returned the Brahmana home and then fetched the rightful Sarmin, whom Yama honoured and sent back with the same instructions; Bhishma adds that lamps for dark places please the Pitris and the gods, that gems and robes bring merit when rightly given, and that a son is the greatest acquisition.

B13C069.summary: Yudhishthira asks again about gifts, especially the gift of earth, and which objects any class may give to earn merit. Bhishma names three gifts of equal worth, kine, earth and knowledge, and says that cows are the mothers of all creatures and must be treated with care. He then explains which cows and which recipients are fit, and warns that a cow should not go to the unrighteous, and that taking a Brahmana's property is as grave as the merit of a cow-gift is great.

scenes.B13C069S01: Yudhishthira's question on which gifts all classes may make, Bhishma's account of kine, earth and knowledge as gifts of equal merit, and his rules on fit recipients.

shots.B13C069S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma again about the rules of gifts, especially the gift of earth, which classes may make gifts, and what the Vedas say.
shots.B13C069S01H02: Bhishma names kine, earth and knowledge as three gifts of equal worth, says that teaching sound lessons to a disciple matches giving earth and kine, and praises cows as mothers of all creatures who must not be kicked or harmed.
shots.B13C069S01H03: Yudhishthira asks which cows are fit to give, which should be passed over, and who should and should not receive them.
shots.B13C069S01H04: Bhishma says cows should not go to the unrighteous, the greedy, liars or those who neglect the Pitris and gods; he praises gifts of ten cows to a learned, poor Brahmana, lists those worthy of support, and warns that robbing a Brahmana is as sinful as giving a cow is meritorious.

B13C070.summary: Bhishma tells the story of king Nriga, who was cursed for taking a cow that had been given to a Brahmana by mistake. Yadava youths find a huge lizard stuck in a well and ask Krishna for help, and the lizard reveals itself as the soul of Nriga. Nriga explains that he gave away a cow that another Brahmana had lost, and that when he offered a hundred thousand cows in exchange, both Brahmanas refused. Yama then punishes him for breaking his oath and taking a Brahmana's property, and Krishna frees him to heaven. Vasudeva's verse on not taking a Brahmana's property closes the tale.

scenes.B13C070S01: The story of king Nriga, the lizard in the well, Nriga's account of his sin, Yama's judgement, and Krishna's rescue and moral.

shots.B13C070S01H01: Bhishma tells how king Nriga was punished for taking a Brahmana's cow: Yadava youths find a huge lizard in a well and bring Krishna, who draws it out and learns it is the soul of Nriga; Nriga confesses that he gave away a cow that another Brahmana had lost, that both Brahmanas refused his offers of many cows, gold and horses; Yama then judged that his sin of breaking his oath and taking a Brahmana's property must be paid for; Nriga fell into the well as a lizard, and Yama had promised that Krishna would rescue him, which he now does, and Krishna then recites the verse that a Brahmana's property destroys the taker and that goodness brings rescue, so one must not harm kine.

B13C071.summary: Yudhishthira asks for more on the merit of giving cows, and Bhishma tells the story of the sage Uddalaki and his son Nachiketa. When Nachiketa cannot find the firewood and ritual items that the current has carried off, his father curses him to meet Yama, and the boy dies; the father's grief brings him back to life. Nachiketa then tells how Yama showed him the heavenly regions of cow-givers, with rivers of milk and ghee, and taught the rules for giving cows, including substitute cows made of ghee, sesame or water when real cows are not available.

scenes.B13C071S01: Yudhishthira's request, the story of Uddalaki and Nachiketa, Nachiketa's visit to Yama and Yama's rules for gifts of cows, and Yama's teaching on substitute cows.

shots.B13C071S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma for more on the merits of giving cows, saying he is never tired of his words.
shots.B13C071S01H02: Bhishma tells of the sage Uddalaki, who sends his son Nachiketa for firewood, Kusa grass, flowers, water and potherbs; the son finds that the current has swept them away, the father curses him to meet Yama, the boy dies, and the father's grief restores him; Nachiketa then describes Yama's realm, its mansions and rivers of milk and ghee, and Yama's rules for gifts of cows.
shots.B13C071S01H03: Nachiketa says Yama taught him substitutes for cows, such as cows made of ghee, sesame or water, and urged him to give cows regularly; Nachiketa says the curse was a blessing that let him see the rewards of giving.

B13C072.summary: Yudhishthira asks about the regions reserved for those who give cows, having heard of Nriga and Nachiketa. Bhishma introduces a dialogue between Brahma and Indra. Indra is puzzled that the residents of the cow-givers' regions outshine the gods of heaven, and asks what those regions are like, how long their rewards last, and how gifts of many cows compare with gifts of a few. The chapter ends with Indra's questions still open.

scenes.B13C072S01: Yudhishthira's question about the regions of cow-givers, and Indra's questions to Brahma about those regions and the merit of many versus few cows.

shots.B13C072S01H01: Yudhishthira asks about the regions reserved for those who give cows, since he has heard of Nachiketa's teaching and of Nriga's fate.
shots.B13C072S01H02: Bhishma introduces a discourse between Brahma and the sacrificer Indra.
shots.B13C072S01H03: Indra says the residents of the cow-givers' regions outshine the gods of heaven and asks what those regions are, what they yield, how long the rewards last, and how gifts of many cows compare with gifts of few.

B13C073.summary: Brahma answers Indra's questions about the regions reserved for cow-givers, describing a realm where time, decay and disease do not reach and where cows roam freely. He lists the virtues needed to reach it, such as forgiveness, obedience to teachers, truthfulness and compassion for kine, and the sins that bar the way. He then sets out the merit of giving cows according to the giver's class and the means of acquiring them, and the rules for choosing recipients and performing the gift.

scenes.B13C073S01: Brahma's description of the cow-givers' regions, the virtues and sins that decide who reaches them, the merit of cow-gifts by class and source, and the rules for recipients and the gift itself.

shots.B13C073S01H01: Brahma tells Indra that the cow-givers' regions are beyond even Indra's sight and describes their qualities, the virtues and vows that lead there, the sins that bar the way, the merit of gifts of cows by class and means, and the rules for choosing recipients and performing the gift; he closes by praising the reverence for cows, and the rewards for a rescuer of cows and Brahmanas.

B13C074.summary: Indra asks what becomes of a man who knowingly steals a cow or sells one for profit. Brahma answers that anyone who kills, eats or sells cows, or lets others slaughter them for gain, will rot in hell for as many years as the cow has hairs, and that a stolen cow given away still brings sin. He adds that gold is the best Dakshina for a cow-gift. Bhishma says this teaching came down from Brahma through Indra, Dasaratha, Rama, Lakshmana and the sages to his own teacher, and he urges Yudhishthira to recite it.

scenes.B13C074S01: Indra's question about cow thieves and sellers, Brahma's answer on the punishments and on gold as Dakshina, and Bhishma's account of how the teaching was handed down.

shots.B13C074S01H01: Indra asks what becomes of a man who knowingly steals a cow or sells one for greed.
shots.B13C074S01H02: Brahma says that killers, eaters and sellers of cows, and those who let them be slaughtered for profit, will rot in hell for as many years as the cow has hairs; a stolen cow given away still brings the punishment for theft; gold is the best Dakshina for cow-gifts, and it rescues the giver's ancestors and descendants.
shots.B13C074S01H03: Bhishma says Brahma taught this to Indra, who taught Dasaratha, who taught Rama, who taught Lakshmana; the sages and righteous kings kept it, and Bhishma's own teacher passed it on to him; whoever recites it at assemblies, sacrifices and gifts of cows gains lasting heaven.

B13C075.summary: Yudhishthira asks what rewards come from vows, study, gifts, the refusal of gifts, teaching, valour in battle, purity, celibacy, service to parents and teachers, and compassion. Bhishma answers that self-restraint is worth more than giving, since a giver may act in anger but a restrained man does not. He describes the honours of teachers, the Vedic students, heroes of many kinds, and the truthful, and he says truth outweighs a thousand horse-sacrifices. He ends with the merits of lifelong celibacy and of serving parents and elders, which keep a man from hell.

scenes.B13C075S01: Yudhishthira's list of questions on the rewards of virtue, and Bhishma's answers on self-restraint, study, heroes, truth, celibacy and service to elders.

shots.B13C075S01H01: Yudhishthira asks about the rewards of vows, study, gifts, the refusal of gifts, teaching, heroism in battle, purity, celibacy, service to parents and teachers, and compassion.
shots.B13C075S01H02: Bhishma says those who keep vows to the end, study the Vedas, and practise self-restraint win lasting honour and happiness; self-restraint outweighs gifts because a giver may be spoiled by anger; he describes the rewards of teachers, students, warriors and gift-givers, names many kinds of heroes, says truth outweighs a thousand horse-sacrifices, and ends by praising lifelong celibacy and service to parents, which spare a man from hell.

B13C076.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma for the exact ritual of giving cows. Bhishma says a lawfully acquired cow given away rescues the giver's whole family and recounts how king Mandhatri asked Vrihaspati for the rite: honour Brahmanas the day before, give cows of the Rohini class, spend the night in the cow-pen with mantras, and give the proper substitutes when a cow is not available. He lists kings who won heaven by following the rite and urges Yudhishthira to do the same. The chapter closes by noting that Yudhishthira obeyed, took up a cow-based diet and simple life, and stopped yoking cattle to his chariots.

scenes.B13C076S01: Yudhishthira's request for the ritual, Bhishma's account of the rite taught to Mandhatri, and Yudhishthira's obedience to it.

shots.B13C076S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to set out in detail the rules that govern gifts of cows, since they lead to lasting heaven.
shots.B13C076S01H02: Bhishma says a lawfully acquired cow given away rescues the giver's family; he recounts how Mandhatri asked Vrihaspati about the rite, which requires honouring Brahmanas, choosing cows of the Rohini class, spending the night in the cow-pen with mantras, giving the cow with a calf and a bull at sunrise, and using substitutes such as the value of a cow, cloth or gold; he gives the rewards for each, and names kings who won heaven by this rite.
shots.B13C076S01H03: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira followed Bhishma's teaching: he gave cows often, lived on barley and dung, slept on bare earth, revered cows, and stopped yoking cattle to his vehicles.

B13C077.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma once more about giving cows, and Bhishma lays down rules on which cows to give: healthy, young, gentle and fragrant ones, with calves, and never sick, dry or unwilling animals. Yudhishthira asks why the tawny Kapila cow is so praised, and Bhishma tells how Daksha made the cow Surabhi from his breath and how her daughters were born from nectar. The story goes on to Mahadeva's angered glance, Daksha's blessing that the milk stays pure, and Mahadeva's becoming lord of cattle, which is why he bears a bull on his standard. Yudhishthira then gives many cows and bulls to Brahmanas.

scenes.B13C077S01: Yudhishthira's second request, Bhishma's rules on the choice of cows, and Yudhishthira's question about the Kapila cow.
scenes.B13C077S02: Bhishma's history of Surabhi and the Kapila cows, the story of Mahadeva and Daksha, and Yudhishthira's gifts to the Brahmanas.

shots.B13C077S01H01: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira again asks Bhishma for the details of cow-gifts.
shots.B13C077S01H02: Yudhishthira says he has not tired of Bhishma's words and asks for more on the merit of giving cows.
shots.B13C077S01H03: Vaisampayana says Bhishma goes on to describe the merit of cow-gifts.
shots.B13C077S01H04: Bhishma says a cow with a calf, gentle and young, wrapped in cloth, cleanses a giver's sins; a sick, dry, weak or unpaid cow should never be given; only strong, well-behaved, fragrant cows are worthy, and the Kapila is the best, as the Ganga is the best river.
shots.B13C077S01H05: Yudhishthira asks why the Kapila cow is especially praised, when all good cows should count alike.
shots.B13C077S02H01: Bhishma tells how Daksha, asked by Brahma to create living things, made food first, and how his breath made the cow Surabhi, whose golden Kapila daughters sustained creatures; froth from their milk fell on Mahadeva, who angered at the milk and glared at the cows; Daksha said the milk stays pure, gave Mahadeva a bull, and Mahadeva became the bull-bannered lord of cattle; Bhishma closes by praising Kapila cow-gifts and their rewards.
shots.B13C077S02H02: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira and his brothers gave bulls and cows of many colours to the Brahmanas, and gave hundreds of thousands of cows in sacrifices.

B13C078.summary: Bhishma tells how king Saudasa of Ikshvaku's line asks his priest Vasishtha which sacred thing, if recited, brings great merit. Vasishtha answers by praising cows as the refuge of all creatures, the source of sacrifice, offerings and prosperity, and says that gifts of cows bring merit in proportion to the giver's devotion. He lists the everyday rules for honouring cows, such as not eating their flesh, never soiling their dung, and saying their names each morning and night, and he ends with the verse-like formula for a safe refuge in cows.

scenes.B13C078S01: Saudasa's question to Vasishtha, Vasishtha's praise of cows, and his rules for honouring them.

shots.B13C078S01H01: Bhishma says that king Saudasa of Ikshvaku's line asked his priest Vasishtha, a great and long-lived sage, what sacred thing brings merit if recited.
shots.B13C078S01H02: Saudasa asks Vasishtha which sacred thing in the three worlds brings great merit when recited at all times.
shots.B13C078S01H03: Vasishtha bows to the cows, purifies himself, and begins to teach the mystery of cows.
shots.B13C078S01H04: Vasishtha praises cows as the refuge of all creatures, the source of sacrifice and prosperity, and the proper food for the gods; he says that gifts to cows and the honour shown to them bring prosperity, and gives rules: never eat their flesh, never soil their dung, bow to them morning and evening, say their names at night and morning, and end every rite and every fear with their names.

B13C079.summary: Vasishtha tells Saudasa how the cows, after a hundred thousand years of penance, asked Brahma for the boon that they would be the finest of gifts and that their dung would purify people; Brahma granted it, and cows became the refuge of the world. He then lists the heavenly regions won by giving cows of different colours, calves, and bulls to particular deities, from Brahma and Surya down to Prajapati. The giver of cows rises to heaven, is attended by celestial women, and returns to earth in a noble family.

scenes.B13C079S01: Vasishtha's account of the cows' penance and boon, and his list of heavenly rewards for giving cows of each colour and to each deity.

shots.B13C079S01H01: Vasishtha tells how the cows of old performed penance, asked Brahma that they become the best gifts and that their dung purify people, received the boon, and became the refuge of the world; he then lists the regions gained by giving cows of various colours and calves, and bulls, to the gods and their realms, and describes the giver's welcome in heaven and his return to a noble family.

B13C081.summary: Yudhishthira asks which is the most sacred thing, and Bhishma says cows, which uphold all creatures and rescue their givers. Bhishma tells how the sage Suka asked his father Vyasa which sacrifice and act is greatest. Vyasa explains that cows were once hornless until they worshipped Brahma, who gave them horns and their desires; he describes the rich land of the cow-givers, and gives mantras, purification by cow products, and the rewards of cow worship. Suka is then said to have worshipped cows every day.

scenes.B13C081S01: Yudhishthira's question, Bhishma's account of cows' sanctity and the cow-givers' rewards, Suka's question to Vyasa and Vyasa's answer on cows, and Bhishma's closing note on Suka.

shots.B13C081S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma for the most sacred of all sacred things.
shots.B13C081S01H02: Bhishma says cows are the foremost of sacred things, that they sustain all creatures with their milk and clarified butter, and that kings like Mandhatri, Yayati and Nahusha gave cows by the thousand; he introduces Suka asking his father Vyasa, called the Island-born Krishna in the text, which sacrifice and act is greatest.
shots.B13C081S01H03: Vyasa says cows are the stay and refuge of creatures; that they were once hornless until they worshipped Brahma, who gave them horns and their wishes; he describes the splendid region of the cow-givers, with its flowers, gems, streams and lakes; he gives mantras, cow-product fasts and the reward of Gomati chants, and says cows can grant any wish when served with reverence.
shots.B13C081S01H04: Bhishma says Suka took his father's words to heart and worshipped cows every day, and urges Yudhishthira to do the same.

B13C082.summary: Yudhishthira asks why cow dung is said to hold Sree, the goddess of fortune. Bhishma tells how Sree came into a herd of cows, dazzled them with her beauty, and asked to dwell in them. The cows first refuse her because she is fickle, then, when she pleads, they grant her a place in their urine and dung. Sree agrees and vanishes, which explains why cow dung is sacred and holds prosperity. Bhishma says he will continue on the glory of cows.

scenes.B13C082S01: Yudhishthira's question, Sree's arrival among the cows, and the cows' first refusal.
scenes.B13C082S02: Sree's plea for a place among the cows, the cows' final offer of urine and dung, and Sree's acceptance.
scenes.B13C082S03: Sree's thanks, her disappearance, and Bhishma's introduction of his next topic.

shots.B13C082S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how cow dung came to hold Sree, the goddess of fortune, and asks Bhishma to explain.
shots.B13C082S01H02: Bhishma introduces a conversation between the cows and Sree, who enters a herd in beautiful form, and the cows are amazed.
shots.B13C082S01H03: The cows ask Sree who she is, where she comes from and where she goes.
shots.B13C082S01H04: Sree says she is dear to all creatures, that she brings success to gods and sages and that she wants to dwell in each cow.
shots.B13C082S01H05: The cows say she is fickle and passed around, so they do not want her, and bid her go elsewhere.
shots.B13C082S02H01: Sree asks why the cows reject her, saying that no one turns her away and that she is hard to win.
shots.B13C082S02H02: The cows say they do not slight her, but she is restless, so they let her go wherever she chooses.
shots.B13C082S02H03: Sree pleads that she will be shunned by all the world if the cows reject her, and offers to dwell even in the most unclean parts of their bodies.
shots.B13C082S02H04: Bhishma says the kind cows took counsel together and then spoke to Sree.
shots.B13C082S02H05: The cows say she should live in their urine and dung, since both are sacred.
shots.B13C082S03H01: Sree thanks the cows, accepts their offer, and agrees to the compact.
shots.B13C082S03H02: Bhishma says Sree vanished before the cows, and that he will now tell more of the glory of cows.

B13C080.summary: Vasishtha gives a mantra that calls cows the source of ghee and milk and asks that they always stay near him, to be recited morning and evening to cleanse daily sins. He describes the heaven reached by those who give a thousand cows, with rivers of milk, curds and cheese. He calls cows the refuge of the universe and says a Kapila cow given with its calf and a brass milking vessel lets the giver pass safely into Yama's realm. Saudasa then gives many cows to Brahmanas and gains many heavens.

scenes.B13C080S01: Vasishtha's mantra in praise of cows and his account of their rewards, followed by Bhishma's note that Saudasa gave many cows and won heavenly regions.

shots.B13C080S01H01: Vasishtha recites a mantra calling cows the source of ghee and milk and asking them to stay near him, says it cleanses daily sins when recited after washing; he describes the rivers of milk and curds that await those who give a thousand cows, calls cows the refuge of the universe, says a Kapila cow given with a calf and brass vessel carries the giver safely past Yama's palace, and says no gift or refuge is higher than the cow.
shots.B13C080S01H02: Bhishma says Saudasa took Vasishtha's words to heart, gave many cows to Brahmanas with restrained senses, and won many regions of felicity.

B13C083.summary: Bhishma says that those who give cows and eat the remnants of the sacred offerings are always counted as sacrificers, since no sacrifice works without ghee. He tells how the gods and sages gathered before Brahma after the Daityas were defeated, and Indra asked why the realm of cows lies above the realm of the gods. Brahma explains that cows are the limbs of sacrifice, sustain creatures, and serve with patience, and that the goddess Surabhi won an eternal realm called Goloka through her austerities. Indra then worships cows every day, and Bhishma says anyone devoted to cows gains his wishes.

scenes.B13C083S01: Bhishma's opening on the sanctity of cows and ghee, Brahma's answer to Indra about the realm of cows, and Surabhi's reward; and Bhishma's closing on the rewards of devotion to cows.

shots.B13C083S01H01: Bhishma says the givers of cows and those who eat the remnants of offerings always sacrifice, since ghee is the root of sacrifice; he tells how the gods and sages honoured Brahma, and how Indra asked why the cows' realm is higher than the gods'; Brahma explains that cows are the limbs of sacrifice, that calves help with tilling, and that Surabhi, daughter of Daksha, won the boon of an eternal realm called Goloka through long austerities; Brahma then tells Indra that the path to that realm is through chastity, penance, truth and gifts.
shots.B13C083S01H02: Bhishma says Indra took up daily worship of cows after hearing Brahma, and that the devoted, men and women alike, gain sons, wealth, learning and happiness; he closes the account of the sanctity of cows.
